6	(which uses the Four-Cell Pattern per script) and extracts each script back
7	into a standalone .py file with its execution log appended — exactly as it
8	existed before notebook assembly.
9	
10	Usage:
11	    python decompile_notebook.py <notebook_path> <output_dir>
12	
13	Example:
14	    python scripts/decompile_notebook.py \
15	        research/2026-02-15_.../2026-02-15_...Analysis.py \
16	        research/2026-03-24_.../original_files/scripts
17	
18	Output:
19	    Creates one .py file per script found in the notebook, organized into
20	    stage subdirectories matching the original layout:
21	        output_dir/stage5_fetch/01_fetch-directory_a.py
22	        output_dir/stage6_clean/01_clean-directory.py
23	        ...
24	
25	Each extracted file contains the un-commented code followed by the execution
26	log re-formatted as comments — a faithful reconstruction of the original
27	executed script file.
28	"""

31	import re

37	    """Split notebook text into individual cell bodies.

39	    Each cell starts with @app.cell followed by a def line.
40	    Returns list of (cell_body, raw_text) tuples.
41	    """
42	    # Split on @app.cell boundaries
43	    parts = re.split(r'\n@app\.cell\n', notebook_text)
44	    # First part is the file header (imports, marimo boilerplate) — skip it
45	    cells = []
46	    for part in parts[1:]:

52	    """Classify a cell as one of: source_code, execution_log, data_inspect,
53	    markdown_header, stage_marker, or unknown.
54	
55	    Returns (cell_type, extracted_content_dict).
56	    """
57	    if '# SOURCE:' in cell_text:
58	        return 'source_code', extract_source_code(cell_text)
59	
60	    if 'mo.accordion({"Execution Log' in cell_text or "mo.accordion({'Execution Log" in cell_text:

62

64	        return 'data_inspect', {}

71	        if '#### ' in cell_text:
72	            return 'markdown_header', extract_header_metadata(cell_text)

75	    return 'unknown', {}

80	    lines = cell_text.split('\n')
81	
82	    source_path = None
83	    code_lines = []
84	    in_code = False
85	    header_lines_remaining = 0
86	
87	    for line in lines:
88	        # Strip the 4-space cell-body indentation
89	        stripped = line[4:] if line.startswith('    ') else line
90

93	            source_path = stripped.replace('# SOURCE:', '').strip()

177	def reconstruct_script(code, log_text):
178	    """Reconstruct an original script file from code and execution log.
179	
180	    Returns the script content as it would have looked after run_with_capture.sh
181	    appended the execution log. Handles both pre-commented and uncommented log
182	    text from notebook accordions (the notebook-assembler may or may not strip
183	    comment prefixes when storing logs in accordion cells).
184	    """
185	    log_lines = log_text.split('\n')
186	
187	    # Detect whether the log text is already comment-prefixed (pre-commented)
188	    # by checking if early lines look like commented execution log markers.
189	    # The known assembler (_build_notebook.py) strips comment prefixes, so
190	    # accordion text is normally plain. But we handle both cases defensively.
191	    is_precommented = False
192	    for line in log_lines[:10]:
193	        stripped = line.strip()
194	        if stripped in ('# EXECUTION LOG', '# ====', '# ====='):
195	            is_precommented = True
196	            break
197	        if stripped.startswith('# ===') and '=' * 10 in stripped:
198	            is_precommented = True
199	            break
200	
201	    if is_precommented:
202	        # Strip existing comment prefixes to normalize, then re-add them.
203	        # This prevents double-commenting (# # EXECUTION LOG).
204	        cleaned_lines = []
205	        for line in log_lines:
206	            if line.startswith('# '):
207	                cleaned_lines.append(line[2:])
208	            elif line == '#':
209	                cleaned_lines.append('')
210	            else:
211	                cleaned_lines.append(line)
212	    else:
213	        # Log text is plain (not pre-commented). Preserve it exactly —
214	        # any '# ' at line starts is genuine content (e.g., Python comments
215	        # captured in stderr), not a comment prefix to strip.
216	        cleaned_lines = log_lines
217	
218	    # Re-comment cleanly (single level of '# ' prefix)
219	    commented_log_lines = []
220	    for line in cleaned_lines:
221	        if line:
222	            commented_log_lines.append('# ' + line)
223	        else:
224	            commented_log_lines.append('#')
225	
226	    commented_log = '\n'.join(commented_log_lines)
227	
228	    # Combine code + execution log
229	    script = code.rstrip()
230	    script += '\n\n\n'
231	
232	    # Ensure the EXECUTION LOG header is present. run_with_capture.sh checks
233	    # for "^# EXECUTION LOG" before allowing re-execution, and the RV-2
234	    # stripping step looks for this marker to remove the log before re-running.
235	    if '# EXECUTION LOG' not in commented_log:
236	        script += '# =============================================================================\n'
237	        script += '# EXECUTION LOG\n'
238	        script += '# =============================================================================\n'
239	
240	    script += commented_log
241	    script += '\n'
242	
243	    return script

2	"""Batch-normalize PROJECT_DIR paths in decompiled scripts.
3	
4	Standalone CLI tool for Reproducibility Verification mode (RV-1).
5	Scans all .py files in a directory tree, finds PROJECT_DIR assignments
6	(both `Path("...")` and plain string `"..."` styles), and rewrites them
7	to point at the reproduction project path.
8	
9	Usage:
10	    python normalize_project_dir.py <scripts_dir> <target_project_dir>
11	
12	Arguments:
13	    scripts_dir         Directory containing decompiled .py scripts
14	    target_project_dir  Absolute path to the reproduction project folder
15	
16	Exit codes:
17	    0  Completed successfully (regardless of whether changes were made)
18	    1  Error (directory not found, no .py files, I/O error)
19	"""
20	
21	import argparse
22	import re
23	import sys
24	from pathlib import Path
25	
26	
27	def find_py_files(scripts_dir):
28	    """Recursively find all .py files under scripts_dir."""
29	    return sorted(scripts_dir.rglob("*.py"))
30	
31	
32	def normalize_file(py_path, target_project_dir):
33	    """Replace PROJECT_DIR = Path("...") or PROJECT_DIR = "..." with the target path.
34	
35	    Matches two patterns:
36	      1. PROJECT_DIR = Path("...")   (pathlib style)
37	      2. PROJECT_DIR = "..."         (plain string style)
38	
39	    Returns (original_value, was_modified, pattern_style) where pattern_style
40	    is 'Path' or 'string' (or None if no match).
41	    """
42	    # Pattern 1: PROJECT_DIR = Path("...")
43	    path_pattern = re.compile(
44	        r"""^(\s*PROJECT_DIR\s*=\s*Path\()(['"])(.*?)\2(\).*)$"""
45	    )
46	    # Pattern 2: PROJECT_DIR = "..." or PROJECT_DIR = '...'
47	    # Must NOT match PROJECT_DIR = Path("...") — negative lookahead for Path(
48	    string_pattern = re.compile(
49	        r"""^(\s*PROJECT_DIR\s*=\s*)(['"])((?:(?!\2).)*)\2(\s*#.*)?$"""
50	    )
51	
52	    text = py_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
53	    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
54	
55	    original_value = None
56	    modified = False
57	    pattern_style = None
58	
59	    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
60	        # Try Path("...") pattern first
61	        m = path_pattern.match(line)
62	        if m:
63	            prefix = m.group(1)      # e.g. 'PROJECT_DIR = Path('
64	            quote = m.group(2)        # ' or "
65	            original_value = m.group(3)
66	            suffix = m.group(4)       # e.g. ')'
67	            pattern_style = 'Path'
68	            if original_value != target_project_dir:
69	                lines[i] = f"{prefix}{quote}{target_project_dir}{quote}{suffix}\n"
70	                modified = True
71	            break
72	
73	        # Try plain string pattern
74	        m = string_pattern.match(line)
75	        if m:
76	            prefix = m.group(1)      # e.g. 'PROJECT_DIR = '
77	            quote = m.group(2)        # ' or "
78	            original_value = m.group(3)
79	            trailing = m.group(4) or ''  # optional inline comment
80	            pattern_style = 'string'
81	            if original_value != target_project_dir:
82	                lines[i] = f"{prefix}{quote}{target_project_dir}{quote}{trailing}\n"
83	                modified = True
84	            break
85	
86	    if modified:
87	        py_path.write_text("".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")
88	
89	    return original_value, modified, pattern_style
90	
91	
92	def main():
93	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
94	        description="Batch-normalize PROJECT_DIR in decompiled scripts."
95	    )
96	    parser.add_argument(

98	        help="Directory containing decompiled .py scripts",
99	    )
100	    parser.add_argument(
101	        "target_project_dir",
102	        help="Absolute path to the reproduction project folder",
103	    )
104	    args = parser.parse_args()
105	
106	    scripts_dir = Path(args.scripts_dir).resolve()
107	    target_project_dir = str(Path(args.target_project_dir).resolve())
108	
109	    if not scripts_dir.is_dir():
110	        print(f"ERROR: scripts_dir is not a directory: {scripts_dir}", file=sys.stderr)
111	        sys.exit(1)
112	
113	    py_files = find_py_files(scripts_dir)
114	    if not py_files:
115	        print(f"ERROR: No .py files found in {scripts_dir}", file=sys.stderr)
116	        sys.exit(1)
117	
118	    # --- Report header ---
119	    print("=" * 72)
120	    print("PROJECT_DIR Batch Normalization Report")
121	    print("=" * 72)
122	    print(f"Scripts directory : {scripts_dir}")
123	    print(f"Target PROJECT_DIR: {target_project_dir}")
124	    print(f"Files scanned     : {len(py_files)}")
125	    print("-" * 72)
126	
127	    # --- Process each file ---
128	    normalized_count = 0
129	    skipped_count = 0
130	    no_match_count = 0
131	
132	    # Collect rows for the Infrastructure Normalizations table
133	    table_rows = []
134	
135	    for py_path in py_files:
136	        rel_path = py_path.relative_to(scripts_dir)
137	        original_value, was_modified, pattern_style = normalize_file(py_path, target_project_dir)
138	
139	        if original_value is None:

141	        elif was_modified:
142	            normalized_count += 1
143	            table_rows.append((str(rel_path), original_value, target_project_dir, pattern_style))
144	            print(f"  NORMALIZED: {rel_path}")

147	        else:
148	            skipped_count += 1

150	
151	    # --- Summary ---
152	    print("-" * 72)
153	    print(f"Normalized : {normalized_count}")
154	    print(f"Unchanged  : {skipped_count}")
155	    print(f"No match   : {no_match_count}")
156	    print()

412	## Boundaries
413	
414	### Infrastructure vs. Substantive Modifications
415	
416	Not all script modifications are equal. The distinction between infrastructure and substantive changes determines reproduction classification:
417	
418	- **Infrastructure modifications:** Path rewrites (`PROJECT_DIR` values), import path adjustments, environment-specific configuration changes (e.g., temp directory paths, platform-specific settings). These are mechanical, deterministic transformations that do not alter the analytical logic. A script that required **only** infrastructure modifications retains **REPRODUCED** status.
419	
420	- **Substantive modifications:** Changes to data transformations, filters, joins, aggregations, statistical methods, analytical logic, or any code that affects output values. These indicate the original script could not reproduce as-is and **must** be classified as **MODIFIED**. Every substantive modification must be documented in the Per-Script Reproduction Results with full justification.
421	
422	The path normalization performed during RV-1 (step 8) is the canonical example of an infrastructure modification. It is applied deterministically to all scripts and documented in the Reproduction Report's Infrastructure Normalizations section.
423	
424	### Always Do
425	- Process ALL scripts in the notebook, even if some fail
426	- Update the Reproduction Report after EVERY script re-execution
427	- Preserve the original project completely untouched
428	- Document ANY modification required to run a script, no matter how small
429	- Use versioned copies (_repro_a.py) for any modifications, following DAAF conventions
430	- Compare against tolerances defined in the Reproduction Report template
431	
432	### Never Do
433	- Modify files in the original project folder
434	- Skip scripts without explicit user approval
435	- Mark a modified script as REPRODUCED (must be MODIFIED)
436	- Write new analysis code — this mode verifies existing code, not creates new
437	- Change the analytical methodology to "improve" results
438	- Suppress or minimize deviations — every deviation is documented
439	
440	### Ask First
441	- Before skipping any script (even if it appears redundant)
442	- Before making modifications to a script that go beyond path fixes
443	- If a deviation pattern suggests a systemic issue (e.g., all data changed)
444	
445	**See also:** `agent_reference/BOUNDARIES.md` § Reproducibility Verification Mode
